text:
alex: Quick Q — where can I find the audit export format for user provisioning events? Need to answer a SOC question: specifically who granted roles, and whether emails/SSNs are redacted in the export. Can we export as CSV? @maria @sahil

maria: We publish the export schema in the GCS bucket `gs://redwood-audit-schemas` (jsonl by default). Event type is `audit.v1.user_change`. Core fields: actor_id, actor_email (redacted by default), target_id, target_email (redacted by default), action, timestamp, details. SSNs are never logged. :lock:

```json
{
  "event_type": "audit.v1.user_change",
  "actor_id": "u_12345",
  "actor_email": "a***@example.com",
  "target_id": "u_67890",
  "target_email": "t***@example.com",
  "action": "grant_role",
  "timestamp": "2026-02-28T15:22:10Z",
  "details": {
    "role_changes": [
      {"role":"admin","change":"granted","by":"u_12345","reason":"onboarding","scope":"org/1"}
    ]
  }
}
```

sahil: Access note — only principals with the `audit_exporter` or `owner` role plus the `logs:export` permission can create exports. Exports can be done from Console or via API using a service account with the IAM role. Also we keep an export audit entry when an export is requested (so "who exported" is itself auditable).

irene: Retention: hosted default is 365 days. Dedicated/private tenants can request custom retention via the compliance flow. Exports for SOC runs should include the export job_id and checksum. Example API pull: 

```bash
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/audit/exports?job_id=exp_20260301_42" > export.jsonl
```

alex: Two quick follow-ups: (1) Is actor_email always redacted, or is there an opt-in for enterprise tenants? (2) What's the exact schema for `role_changes` inside `details`?

maria: Enterprise tenants can opt-in (via DPA + KMS) to retain PII in logs; in that case emails are encrypted at rest and only visible to org admins who have decrypt rights. The `role_changes` is an array of objects: `[{"role":"<role>","change":"granted|revoked","by":"<actor_id>","reason":"...","scope":"<scope>"}]`. Example event (jsonl):

```json
{"event_type":"audit.v1.user_change","actor_id":"u_1","actor_email":"alice@example.com","target_id":"u_2","action":"grant_role","timestamp":"2026-02-28T15:22:10Z","details":{"role_changes":[{"role":"engineer","change":"granted","by":"u_1","reason":"project access","scope":"project/123"}]}}
```

audit-bot: Retention policy summary: hosted=365d, dedicated=custom. Exports are recorded (exports_audit_trail=true). To request an export open a ticket in #help-security or run `/request-export` in the console.

sahil: If SOC needs CSV quickly we usually transform jsonl -> csv with `jq`. Example transform: 

```bash
jq -r '. | [.timestamp, .actor_email, .action, (.details.role_changes[]? | .role), (.details.role_changes[]? | .change)] | @csv' export.jsonl > audit_roles.csv
```

irene: I will grant alex a temporary `audit_exporter` scoped to 4 hours. Alex, confirm when you finish so I can revoke. :white_check_mark:

alex: Thanks — will pull the export, run the transform, and share the redacted CSV with SOC. Will ping here when done.
